- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is rising, cap the upward trend at 1–2% above recent low to prevent overcorrection.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (prices trending down from highs), adjust forecast to reflect a 1–3% downward bias in the final 7–10 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3), avoid overfitting to recent highs/lows; use 3–5 day moving average as a smoothing anchor.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true price by 2–4% in the first 7 days of the horizon, apply a 1–2% downward correction to early days, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, if sentiment is weak or mixed, reduce forecast slope to match historical 30-day mean reversion rate (typically 0.8–1.2% per day).
